kept.title: Unbounded Buffer Accumulation via `Buffer.concat`
kept.description: In `bench/createMultipartBufferForEncodingBench.js`, the `createMultipartBufferForEncodingBench` function fills an array with `amount` copies of a buffer and performs `Buffer.concat`. An attacker providing a large `amount` via benchmark parameters can cause a heap memory exhaustion.
steps_to_exploit: Identify an endpoint or process using `createMultipartBufferForEncodingBench`.
Submit a request with an extremely large `amount` argument.
Monitor process memory usage until OOM crash.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via uncontrolled memory consumption.

kept.title: Use of Potentially Insecure `Buffer.allocUnsafe`
kept.description: The codebase frequently uses `Buffer.allocUnsafe` (e.g., in `bench/dicer/dicer-bench-multipart-parser.js`). If this memory is not explicitly overwritten before being exposed or used in network responses, it may leak sensitive data from previous allocations.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger the code path that uses `Buffer.allocUnsafe`.
Observe if the buffer is sent directly to an output stream without being fully initialized.
Analyze the returned binary data for memory leaks.
kept.impact: Information disclosure of previously handled sensitive process memory.

kept.title: Potential Path Traversal in filename handling
kept.description: While `basename.js` exists, `lib/types/multipart.js` conditionally uses `basename`. If `preservePath` is set to true, the input filename from the multipart header is used directly, which may allow path traversal if not handled carefully in the downstream application.
steps_to_exploit: Configure Busboy with `preservePath: true`.
Craft a multipart request where the `filename` header contains directory traversal sequences like `../../etc/passwd`.
Observe if the application writes files to unauthorized locations.
kept.impact: Arbitrary file write/overwrite on the server.

kept.title: Unbounded Header Accumulation
kept.description: The `HeaderParser` relies on `maxHeaderPairs` and `maxHeaderSize`, but if the configuration is missing or malformed, it defaults to values that might still be too large for some environments, potentially leading to memory pressure.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a request with thousands of small headers.
Observe if the server buffers the entire header block in memory.
Exhaust memory to force a crash.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) by memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Lack of Explicit Character Set Sanitization
kept.description: In `lib/utils/decodeText.js`, the `other` decoder uses `.bind(charset)`. If `charset` is user-controlled via a `Content-Type` header, it could lead to unexpected behavior in string conversion or potential prototype pollution in some JS environments.
steps_to_exploit: Inject a malicious string into the charset parameter of the Content-Type header.
Observe if the application attempts to use this string as a function or object property.
Trigger potential logic errors or crash.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via object creation
kept.description: In `HeaderParser.js`, `this.header = Object.create(null)` is used correctly, but other parts of the parser logic operate on object properties which could be vulnerable if deep merged or assigned from untrusted sources.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a multipart header payload that mimics internal object properties (e.g., `__proto__`).
Pass this through the parsing logic.
Observe if the application state is altered by the injected property.
kept.impact: Unexpected application state modification or remote code execution (RCE) in specific contexts.

kept.title: Insecure `npm` script usage
kept.description: The `benchmarks/regenerate.cmd` script and `package.json` scripts encourage running code as Administrator and installing multiple node versions locally, which introduces a high attack surface for local environment compromise.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker gains local access.
Uses the script to install malicious Node versions.
Executes the benchmark to trigger local system-level actions.
kept.impact: Privilege escalation and persistence on the development or build machine.

kept.title: Sensitive data in console output
kept.description: In `bench/parse-params.js`, any errors encountered during benchmarking are logged to the console using `console.error(e)`. This could include sensitive payload data if the benchmarked function fails.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an error in the parser.
Observe `console.error` output.
Extract sensitive data from the logs.
kept.impact: Sensitive information disclosure through log files.

kept.title: Weak Randomness in file naming
kept.description: In `lib/utils/basename.js` (and the `parted` dependency), file renaming uses `Math.random().toString(36)`. This is not cryptographically secure and can be predicted, potentially allowing an attacker to guess uploaded filenames.
steps_to_exploit: Determine the predictable pattern of the file naming algorithm.
Upload a file.
Predict the resulting path and attempt to access it before the legitimate user.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive user uploads.

kept.title: Potential Integer Overflow in byte accounting
kept.description: In `lib/types/multipart.js`, byte counts are accumulated using standard JavaScript numbers. While JS numbers support large integers, extreme file sizes could theoretically lead to precision loss in edge-case arithmetic operations.
steps_to_exploit: Upload files of near-limit sizes repeatedly.
Monitor if byte counters diverge from actual bytes received.
Trigger potential logic flaws in limit enforcement.

kept.title: Insecure regex usage in parseParams
kept.description: The `parseParams` function uses a complex regular expression `RE_ENCODED` and manual state-machine parsing to decode parameters. Complex regexes on user input can sometimes lead to catastrophic backtracking.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a crafted string with many encoded segments that trigger regex backtracking.
Monitor CPU usage to observe a DoS condition.

kept.title: Improper cleanup of event listeners
kept.description: The `Multipart.parser.on` listener for parts (or other components) is sometimes not cleaned up correctly upon error, leading to memory leaks over time.
steps_to_exploit: Continuously send malformed multipart requests that trigger errors.
Observe if event listener counts increase in the process.

kept.title: Reliance on `Buffer.from(string, 'binary')`
kept.description: Use of the 'binary' encoding in Node.js is deprecated/discouraged as it does not correctly handle multi-byte characters and can lead to data corruption.
steps_to_exploit: Send data with non-ASCII characters.
Observe if the data is corrupted during processing in `UrlEncoded.prototype.write`.

kept.title: Missing Error Handling in stream write
kept.description: In `benchmarks/busboy/contestants/busboy.js`, the call to `busboy.write(buffer, () => { })` passes an empty callback. If an error occurs, it is not properly caught, potentially leaving the stream in an inconsistent state.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an error during a write operation.
Observe if the process fails to handle the stream error gracefully.

kept.title: Default to unsafe charset handling
kept.description: The parser defaults to `utf8` if a charset is missing, which may be inappropriate for legacy systems or specific binary formats, potentially leading to security bypasses in downstream applications expecting stricter encoding controls.
steps_to_exploit: Send data with a non-standard charset without specifying it.
Observe how the application processes the bytes.
Exploit potential interpretation mismatches.
kept.impact: Security logic bypasses due to character set misinterpretation.
